bullets.title: S&P futures surge 1.7%; semis lead with SOXX +4.5% as AI trade rebounds
bullets.body: S&P 500 E-Mini futures up ~1.7% to 7,318 heading into Friday's shortened session, with the semiconductor ETF (SOXX) up 4.45%. Optical/datacom names led (COHR +8.1%, LITE +7.9%) alongside broader infrastructure plays. 10-year yield ticked up 4bps to 4.90% and WTI crude rose 1.66% to $85.07.

bullets.title: NVDA rally driven by Jensen Congressional testimony expectations; Blackwell China installs briefly weigh
bullets.body: Markets are pricing an administration-friendly reception for Jensen Huang's upcoming Congressional appearance, driving a risk-on AI recovery. A mid-morning headwind emerged when reports surfaced that Chinese firms used NVDA Blackwell GB300/GB200 hardware as loan collateral in Shanghai, briefly softening E-Mini futures at 6:44am ET before stabilizing.

bullets.title: NVIDIA halting shipments to SE Asia; TSMC/Samsung pause <16nm China orders on new US export controls
bullets.body: NVIDIA has instructed brand partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia — a region hosting >50% Chinese hyperscaler demand within Malaysia's 10GW data center plan alone. Separately, TSMC and Samsung halted shipments of sub-16nm products designed by Chinese firms under new BIS restrictions, closing a loophole through which Chinese CSPs accessed ~24% of AI compute via regional data centers.

bullets.title: Piper: SPX still below key MAs; 7,350–7,400 must hold as confirmation; 5.25% yield the bear case trigger
bullets.body: Piper Sandler notes major averages remain under 50- and 200-day moving averages with intermediate breadth on sell signals. A decisive close above 7,350–7,400 would confirm a durable low targeting 7,507; a break below 7,002 reopens 6,970 and 6,882. Rising yields toward 5.25% are flagged as the key downside risk.

bullets.title: Bearish macro view: US stocks down 9 of last 10 days; VXN 36; this bounce is 'exit liquidity'
bullets.body: Keith McCullough frames the current rally as a bear market bounce (the fifth in KOSPI since October) driven by China's National Team buying. NASDAQ Vol (VXN) sits at 36 with a risk range of 30–46, and his 10yr UST range is 4.80–5.01%. He is positioning long bonds into Q4 2026/H1 2027 and warns chasers get crushed.

bullets.title: ECB set for two more hikes; IG Metall deal locks in benign 2028 wage path
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects two further ECB rate hikes near-term after October minutes showed a 'large number' of GC members were prepared to hike. The IG Metall 25-month deal locks in 2.0–2.3% annual wage growth, reinforcing a weak 2028 wage trajectory and supporting eventual policy reversal. Eurozone consumers lifted 1yr inflation expectations to 3.5% from 3.1%.

bullets.title: Euro area confidence softening; France and Spain November flash CPI drop partly seasonal
bullets.body: The European Commission ESI fell 0.7pt to 95.8 in November (consensus 97.2), dragged by Italy (-3.1pt) and France (-2.3pt). French and Spanish HICP flash prints fell 0.5–0.8pt respectively, but JPMorgan attributes much of the core decline to Black Friday discounting rather than structural disinflation, forecasting Eurozone core at 2.5% vs 2.6% prior.

bullets.title: Tokyo core CPI hits 16-month high; BOJ December hike expectations firming
bullets.body: Tokyo core CPI rose to its highest level in 16 months, bolstering the case for a BOJ rate hike at the December meeting. Asian markets rallied sharply in sympathy with global risk-on: Nikkei +2.11%, Hang Seng +2.11%, Shanghai +3.73%, the latter driven by China industrial profits jumping 20.1% y/y in October — the fastest since May.

bullets.title: China 2027 outlook: 4.5% GDP growth, K-shaped recovery; housing enters year 6 of downturn
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts China GDP at 4.5% in 2027 (from 4.6% in 2026), with AI/exports resilient but housing facing 20–30% further activity declines and PPI returning to deflation mid-2027. Trade surplus widens to ~$1.4tn; Section 301/232 tariffs of up to 20% possible before G20. Consumer recovery remains constrained by weak household balance sheets and elevated youth unemployment.

bullets.title: DRAM supply/demand tightens in 2027 then loosens in 2028; NAND facing 20–25% ASP declines in 4Q27
bullets.body: TrendForce revised 1Q27 conventional DRAM contract price gains down to +3–8% QoQ from +5–10%, with prices mostly flat in 2H27 and broad-based declines beginning 1Q28 (bear case: >15% QoQ). 2027 NAND bit supply growth of 29% far exceeds demand growth of 19%, with 4Q27 ASPs seen -20–25% YoY. HBM bit demand still grows ~80% YoY in 2027 with procurement largely locked in.

bullets.title: Agentic AI workloads surged from <10% to ~80% of token consumption since February; compute demand 5x supply
bullets.body: Goldman/Citi note agentic AI workload share of token consumption jumped from under 10% in February to roughly 80% in October, driving infrastructure bottlenecks where compute demand is estimated at 5x available supply. Texas TCEQ resumed data center permitting after a directive from outgoing Governor Abbott's office.

bullets.title: ASML faces geopolitical pressure as Netherlands resists US MATCH Act DUV restrictions
bullets.body: The Dutch Trade Minister is openly opposing US efforts to extend MATCH Act restrictions to DUV immersion machines, calling such measures a threat to Europe's most valuable company. ASML derives ~20% of revenues from China, and enforcement of the US Foreign Direct Product Rule remains a live risk if the Netherlands does not comply voluntarily.

bullets.title: US holiday electronics demand resilient; smartphones split 42/42 Apple/Samsung; gaming hardware #2 at 44%
bullets.body: Citi's holiday survey shows US electronics spending flat YoY but concentrated in smartphones (Apple iPhone and Samsung Galaxy tied at 42% each), gaming hardware/peripherals (44% interest, outranking TVs), and tablets/PCs. Foldable device intent reached 22%, with Samsung dominating that segment.

bullets.title: SAP cutting ~10% of workforce (10,000 roles) in AI restructuring; €3bn savings, FCF headwind
bullets.body: Unconfirmed reports indicate SAP is planning at least 10,000 role cuts representing ~9% of its workforce, with €3bn in potential savings. However, severance costs could hit 2026 FCF by ~€3bn against a €10bn consensus. SAP is also dealing with an active IT security incident in which attackers used agentic AI to steal employee GitHub authentication tokens.

bullets.title: EM equity flows: passive inflows persist despite MSCI EM -16.5%; Taiwan bleeds $65bn in 7 weeks
bullets.body: EM equity inflows slowed to $767mn in the latest week (from $2.4bn prior), marking eight consecutive weeks of positive flows during the worst drawdown over any inflows streak in MSCI EM history. Taiwan saw $6.8bn in outflows (seventh straight week, $65bn+ net redemptions total) while India accelerated to +$3.3bn.

bullets.title: JPM European quant: crash phase likely over; near-term rebound expected but 2027 drift risk remains
bullets.body: JPMorgan's European quant strategy identifies three phases — Crash (complete), Rebound (imminent), Drift lower (2027 risk). Long-short Momentum is down 17.2% since April 10, Global Equity Sentiment Indicator is at recessionary lows, and EPS revisions have peaked. Post-Thanksgiving-to-year-end seasonality supports the near-term bounce, but the team stays pro-risk Value/Small Cap only tactically.

bullets.title: Fed blackout begins ahead of Dec 18 FOMC; S&P tracking for third straight monthly decline
bullets.body: The Federal Reserve enters its pre-meeting blackout period with the December 18 FOMC as the next key catalyst. Despite Friday's risk-on mood, the S&P 500 is on track for its third consecutive monthly decline. The market closes at 1pm ET and bond markets at 2pm ET for the Thanksgiving-shortened session.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike acquires Zscaler in $44B deal; cybersecurity consolidation accelerates
bullets.body: CrowdStrike announced a $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (Nov 23), a major consolidation move in enterprise cybersecurity. Separately, Zscaler was downgraded to Neutral from Outperform at Macquarie. Tech outages and cybersecurity incidents are broadly driving increased opex/capex budgets in enterprise IT.

bullets.title: Key upcoming earnings: MDB, MRVL, CRM reporting Dec 1–2; consensus sets the bar
bullets.body: Marvell (Dec 1, consensus EPS $1.10, revenue $3.15B), MongoDB (Dec 1, EPS $1.61, revenue $762.5M), and Salesforce (Dec 2, EPS $3.45, revenue $11.46B) are the key tech names reporting next week. JPMorgan previews CRM expecting ~11% organic cRPO growth and a F4Q guide of 12%+ as the signal for 2H re-acceleration; Agentforce ARR at $1.5B.
